newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt wins three confidence votes on budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt wins three confidence votes on budget.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government won three confidence votes on its 1997 budget on Monday and pushed the bulk of the bill through to approval in a Senate (upper house) left semi-deserted by an opposition boycott.

The confidence votes covered three so-called umbrella amendments, which group together all the articles of the budget bill, and swept aside some 3,000 amendments submitted by the opposition to delay its passage.
Victory on all three confidence votes was by 166-0 with one abstention.
A subsequent vote on the main body of the budget, which aims to cut next year's deficit by 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion), was won by the government by 164 votes to nil.
The main opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance and the separatist Northern League boycotted the 315-member upper house in protest against the budget and the government's tactics.
"We can't vote on the budget because you won't let us," Enrico Loggia, leader in the Senate of media mogul Silvio Berlusconi's Forza Italia party, said in a speech to the assembly before the walkout.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government hopes to have the remaining two items of the budget bill approved by the Senate by Wednesday.
The package returns to the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) for a final reading which the government hopes will be completed by December 23.
Under Italian law, both houses must approve the budget by December 31 to avoid costly provisional spending measures which the government says would wreck Italy's financial credibility.
The budget is designed to enable Italy to meet some of the tough economic criteria laid down for countries wishing to join the single European currency from its planned start in 1999.
Opposition parties support monetary union (EMU) but have criticised the government for the tax hikes included in the 1997 budget as well as its plans to overhaul the fiscal system.
